display.purpose: Page titles via PageContainer's pageTitle prop only.

label.purpose: Uppercase table headers and field labels, always with muted-foreground.

mono.purpose: Every runtime number, IP, MAC, hostname, timestamp; paired with tabular-nums.

micro.purpose: Dense sub-labels inside cards/nodes/tables (interface names, captions) where body text is too loud.

shadows.name: modal-shadow
shadows.purpose: Modals/dialogs only - the sole layer allowed a real drop shadow, since it must separate from the whole page.

motion.name: transition-standard
motion.purpose: Hover and focus state changes on buttons, tabs, and table rows.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Physical press feedback on buttons and icon controls.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action: apply config, send command, confirm.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #000000; color: #ffffff; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; border: none; transition: background-color 0.15s, transform 0.1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #000000; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost / Secondary Button
components.description: Secondary action sitting next to a primary button (e.g. cancel, define device).
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: #f0f0f0; color: #000000; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; border: 1px solid #ebebeb; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #e0e0e0; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #000000; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: KPI Row
components.description: Signature dense status-line component: dot + icon + label + right-aligned mono value + caption. Replaces equal metric-card grids across every overview-style page.

components.css: .ds-kpi-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #ebebeb; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; } .ds-kpi-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: #000000; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-kpi-icon { width: 14px; height: 14px; color: #000000; opacity: 0.8; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-kpi-label { flex: 1; font-size: 11px; color: #707070; } .ds-kpi-values { text-align: right; } .ds-kpi-value { font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-kpi-caption { font-size: 10px; color: #707070; }

components.name: Status Dot + Label
components.description: The only way device/connection state is shown in tables and lists - never a colored pill background.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; } .ds-status-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-status-online { background: #10b981; } .ds-status-warning { background: #f59e0b; } .ds-status-offline { background: oklch(0.63 0.19 23.03); }

components.name: Data Table
components.description: Dense operational table: muted uppercase header, hairline row dividers, hover highlight.
components.css: .ds-table { width: 100%; text-align: left; font-size: 12px; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; border-collapse: collapse; } .ds-table thead tr { background: #f7f7f7; color: #707070; text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; font-weight: 700; border-bottom: 1px solid #ebebeb; } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { padding: 12px 16px; } .ds-table tbody tr { border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(235,235,235,0.5); transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-table tbody tr:hover { background: rgba(240,240,240,0.4); }

narrative.overview: NetOpsWan is what a network operator opens when a branch office's connection is degraded and they need the answer in seconds, not an aesthetic experience to admire. The system commits to a near-total monochrome base — pure black ink on near-white paper, one grayscale ramp for every surface and border — so that the only colors ever visible on screen are load-bearing signals: emerald for healthy, amber for attention, red for critical, sky/violet reserved for the two series of a traffic chart. Nothing decorative competes with that signal. This is deliberately unglamorous: dense data, mono-spaced numbers, short Turkish labels, and tables that scan fast under fluorescent light, not marketing gloss. It targets, and is explicitly judged against, the operational quality bar of a commercial SD-WAN console (Meraki-class), while looking nothing like a SaaS marketing site.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome-first: black/white/gray is the entire base palette; every other color is a status signal, never decoration.
Flat, bordered surfaces — depth comes from a 1px hairline and a muted-tint background shift, not shadows.
Dense, list-like KPI rows instead of grids of equal cards.
Every numeric value is monospaced and uses tabular-nums.
Turkish-first copy; sentence case, no marketing adjectives.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Color exists only to report device/connection/security state. If a color doesn't map to online/warning/critical/info, it doesn't belong on screen. A status dot plus a matching icon tint is the standard way to say it — never a colored card background.

rules.name: The Tabular Truth Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change at runtime (CPU %, RTT, byte counters, uptime) is rendered in Geist Mono with tabular-nums. A static label never is.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Card separation is a 1px hairline border plus a one-step background shift. Reach for box-shadow only on floating/overlay layers (modals, dropdowns) that sit above the whole page, never on inline panels.

dos: Do put every runtime-changing number in Geist Mono with tabular-nums.
Do use the five status colors (emerald/amber/red/sky/violet) exclusively for state — device health, log severity, chart series — never as page decoration.
Do use a dense KpiRow list instead of a row of three or four equal metric cards.
Do give every interactive element a visible focus-visible ring and an active:scale-[0.98] press state.
Do replace loading spinners with skeleton blocks shaped like the real content.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue outside the five status colors, even for "branding."
Don't use box-shadow on an inline page panel — depth comes from the border + background-tint pairing only (modals/dropdowns are the sole exception).
Don't write a manual <h1> page header — always route the title through PageContainer's pageTitle/pageDescription/pageHeaderAction props so every page's header matches.
Don't use marketing adjectives or exclamation points in status/error copy; Turkish, direct, sentence case.
